topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the learning outcomes regarding the hallmarks of cancer and their underlying genetic mechanisms.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and oncogenic signaling cascades
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in growth factor receptors and downstream signaling pathways enable cancer cells to sustain proliferation independently of external growth cues.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations disrupt normal cell differentiation, trapping cells in immature and highly proliferative states across different cancer types.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how alterations in p53 and the balance of Bcl-2 family proteins enable cancer cells to avoid apoptotic cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and senescence bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how telomere shortening and cellular stress induce senescence and how cancer cells bypass these controls to achieve unlimited replicative potential.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the transition to complex cancer hallmarks and how tumor cells rewire their metabolic pathways to support rapid proliferation through aerobic glycolysis and oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how growing tumors overcome nutrient and oxygen diffusion limits by triggering new blood vessel formation.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and secondary colonization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biological steps, microenvironmental factors, clinical monitoring, and genomic characteristics involved in cancer cell invasion and metastatic colonization.

topics.label: Conclusion and lecture summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing remarks on synthesizing the hallmarks of cancer and information about upcoming practical sessions.
